newsitem.title: UK: ENGLISH PASTOR DEFENDS MEMORIAL SERVICE FOR MONKEY.
newsitem.headline: ENGLISH PASTOR DEFENDS MEMORIAL SERVICE FOR MONKEY.

text.p: An Anglican priest is defending the use of his church for a memorial service for a pet monkey called Bill.
The pet regularly shared meals with his grieving owners who described Bill as a luxury-loving "human" with his personal colour TV, along with regular pots of tea like any English citizen.
The Reverend Stephen Prior agreed to hold the service at St Mary and St Cuthbert's church in Chester-le-Street, northeast England, after the death of the 25-year-old monkey
Sam and Shirley Bruce bought him off a photographer using him as a prop for snaps of holidaymakers at the northern resort town of Blackpool.

"Bill didn't want his photograph taken, he wanted a life of luxury, which we gave him. We bought him toys for his birthday and Christmas. When we were happy, he was happy. When we were sad, he put his arms round us," Shirley Bruce told The Times newspaper.
She said Bill was one of the family. "He was human. He did everything we did. He cleaned his teeth, he had his own colour telly, he had his own little bed and blankets.
The congregation at the service, sang hymns and listened to music from the Disney film, The Lion King."I wanted him to have a proper funeral," Shirley said.
Prior said it had not been a funeral ceremony, but a service of commemoration for all creatures. "No animal or coffin was brought into the church... We filled a pastoral need," he said.
